## 01 · Triggers

Daily schedule and manual webhook entry point.

Both paths run through the same RSS ingestion pipeline, so manual tests exercise the production logic without maintaining a separate test flow.

## 02 · Cybersecurity Sources

Security-focused RSS feeds are grouped here for clear ownership and easier troubleshooting.

Each source is kept as a dedicated node. Category-level Merge nodes consolidate related feeds before the global merge, making it simple to disable, replace, or debug a single provider.

## 03 · AI, Research & Semiconductors

AI labs, research outlets, cloud/infra sources, and NVIDIA feeds are grouped separately from cybersecurity and general tech.

This keeps topic balance visible and prevents a single domain from dominating the final briefing.

## 04 · General Technology Sources

Broad technology coverage from TechCrunch, Ars Technica, Wired, The Verge, and Reuters Tech.

These feeds provide wider industry context and are merged separately before joining the global article stream.

## 05 · Merge, Filter, Sort, Normalize

All topic streams converge into `Merge_All`.

The pipeline then keeps recent items only, sorts by publication date, deduplicates, caps noisy sources, and normalizes every article into a single `articles` array for downstream AI processing.

## 06 · Reliable AI Generation Chain

Primary: OpenAI AI Agent for the production-quality briefing.

Fallback: Gemini with retry/backoff when the primary path fails.

Final safety net: deterministic HTML renderer fallback, so provider rate limits or malformed LLM output never block delivery.

## 07 · Render & Delivery

The renderer converts structured AI output into the final responsive HTML newsletter.

Subscribers are loaded from Google Sheets, validated, and delivered through Mailgun. Test sends should temporarily route to an explicit single recipient only.
